does_not_establish: that any new bath exists in nature
that morphology or clumping alone is evidence of dissipation
historical novelty of open-system memory kernels
historical novelty relative to extended-satellite dynamical-friction fits or dissipative-dark-matter cooling and collapse
a real-data fit or independent confirmation
that ordinary cooling, shocks, dynamical friction, violent relaxation or feedback have been excluded
establishes: six receiver-bearing capture models and two mandatory conservative controls with explicit energy, momentum, angular-momentum and irreversibility ledgers
exact frozen examples separating true capture from conservative focusing
a target-blind public TNG hydrodynamic-versus-collisionless falsification plan
a novel candidate signature: history-conditioned capture and two-timescale persistence at the same instantaneous encounter state

predictions: At fixed mass ratio, pericenter, gas fraction and pre-encounter structure, normalized integrated EnergyDissipation plus radiative cooling predicts a larger decrease in visible relative orbital energy and a shorter coalescence time.

At matched instantaneous separation, relative speed, mass ratio and gas fraction, post-pericenter systems have a larger residual loss rate than first-infall systems only for a memory bath; an instantaneous shock law has no history residual after its measured gas state is controlled.

The bimodal bath predicts a fast approximately one-Gyr decay and a distinct slow persistence tail in phase-space distance; the frozen constants are calibrated only to the published one-object Illustris benchmark and must be tested without retuning on TNG100-1.
Any visible orbital angular-momentum deficit must be balanced by gas/internal spin, outflow or radiative flux within the declared aperture ledger.

A matched TNG100-1-Dark history can show collisionless mixing and clumping without positive gas receiver flux; morphology or phase-space persistence alone is therefore insufficient evidence for dissipation.

The candidate must outperform Newtonian time-dependent collisionless evolution, standard shock/cooling, the Boylan-Kolchin extended-satellite merger-time law, dissipative-DM cooling/gravothermal-collapse models, and flexible history controls before a new-gravity interpretation is considered.

strongest_counterexample.required_control: Matched TNG100-1-Dark assembly history and explicit total-energy ledger.
strongest_counterexample.statement: A time-dependent but conservative collisionless potential redistributes particle energies and angular momenta and can leave long-lived clumping or phase-space memory without a new dissipative receiver.

strongest_lead.next_falsifier: Target-blind TNG100-1 versus TNG100-1-Dark major-merger histories with no retuning of the published-benchmark-calibrated persistence constants.
strongest_lead.novelty_boundary: The bath and sum-of-exponentials are known structures, extended-satellite friction already predicts merger times, and dissipative dark sectors already cool and collapse; only a universal gravity activation plus same-current-state fast/slow receiver-flux hysteresis that beats those controls could support application-level novelty.
